title: 10 Science Facts That Sound Fake but Have Real Explanations
description: An educational deep dive into science.
script: Section 1. Science becomes memorable when a surprising claim is paired with the mechanism behind it. Lightning can briefly heat air beyond the temperature of the Sun's visible surface, but temperature is not the same as total energy. Clouds can contain enormous masses of liquid water because tiny droplets are distributed through huge volumes. GPS depends on relativistic clock corrections. Deep-ocean machines need to resist immense pressure. Each example becomes less mysterious once scale, measurement, and mechanism are explained. The practical takeaway from this section is to distinguish the memorable headline from the evidence and mechanism behind it. Examples are useful starting points, but context determines whether a general principle applies to a particular case. Section 2.
